To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hardware impairments can significantly degrade the performance of the frequency localized waveforms, and the degradation can be even larger than that of OFDM.
the low out-of-band advantage of FBMC, UF-OFMD, and W/P-OFMD over OFDM may vanish when hardware impairmens are considered.
The performance of 5G waveform candidates degrades significantly when hardware impairments (e.g., phase noise) are considered.
In summary, our research is concerned with
evaluating various 5G waveform candidates considering realistic hardware impairments and high carrier frequencies.
the evaluation of the waveform performance in the presence of hardware impairments and above 5 GHz operation.
evaluating the performance of various 5G waveforms under realistic hardware impairments for above 6 GHz operation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the waveforms is not significantly impacted by the hardware impairments, but the performance of the waveform is significantly impacted by the waveform itself.
OFDM and DTF-OFDM are still the best candidates in this regard.
OFDM and DTSF-OFDM waveforms are more robust to hardware impairments than the frequency localized waveforms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the waveform selection for 5G is not a simple matter of choosing the waveform with the best performance in the absence of hardware impairments, but also requires the consideration of hardware impairments.
, in the presence of hardware impairments, the performance of OFDM and DTS-OFDM is not degraded significantly and these waveforms can be considered as potential candidates.

the performance of a waveform depends on the specific scenario (e.g., hardware impairments, carrier frequency, bandwidth, etc.) and the waveform design should be optimized for the targeted application.
The main takeaway from our work is that
waveform design for 5G must consider hardware impairments and above 60GHz operation.
the performance evaluation of the 5G waveform candidates at high carrier frequencies needs to be done considering the impact of the hardware impairments.
waveform design for 5G should consider realistic hardware impairments and the potential operation at above 6 GHz carrier frequencies.
